description: The plot illustrates the training loss as a function of total floating-point operations (TFLOPs) for two models: “Vanilla” (purple line with triangle markers) and “SepLLM” (red line with circle markers), as presented in the paper “SepLLM: Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into One Separator.” The x-axis, labeled “TFLOPs,” spans from 0.00 to 1.25 × 10⁹, with major tick marks at intervals of 0.25 × 10⁹. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” ranges from 2.40 to 2.75, with tick marks at 0.05 intervals. Both lines show a decreasing trend in loss as TFLOPs increase, indicating improved model performance with more computation. The “Vanilla” model starts at approximately 2.77 at 0.00 TFLOPs and declines to about 2.50 at 1.25 × 10⁹ TFLOPs. The “SepLLM” model begins at roughly 2.75 and drops more steeply, reaching approximately 2.47 at 1.25 × 10⁹ TFLOPs. A green dashed box highlights the region from 1.00 to 1.25 × 10⁹ TFLOPs, with a label “1.28×” indicating that SepLLM achieves the same loss as Vanilla at 1.28× fewer TFLOPs — specifically, SepLLM reaches a loss of ~2.50 at ~1.00 × 10⁹ TFLOPs, while Vanilla requires ~1.28 × 10⁹ TFLOPs to reach the same loss. A horizontal green dashed line at Loss = 2.50 visually anchors this comparison.
